title: Café Touba, AeroPress with Toasted Selim
author: Julia Bobak (Home Grounds)
desc: 15 g of medium-fine ground coffee, one Selim pepper pod toasted in a dry pan until it smells, ground and used by the half teaspoon in an AeroPress topped up with 200 °F water and steeped 2 to 3 minutes.
longDesc: Julia Bobak’s Home Grounds recipe, published 16 August 2022 and last updated 27 June 2025, yields one 8-ounce drink. The spices — one Selim pepper pod, and optionally 1 teaspoon grated nutmeg, 1 teaspoon coriander seeds and 1 cardamom pod — are toasted in a dry pan over medium heat ‘until they release their aroma’, stirring occasionally to avoid burnt spots, then ground in a spice grinder or mortar to about the size of the coffee grounds. 15 g of medium-fine ground coffee goes in an AeroPress with a fine metal or paper filter, with only 1/2 teaspoon of the ground spice mix; water of at least 16 ounces is boiled, the chamber is topped with 200 °F water and steeped 2 to 3 minutes. The traditional version uses dark-roasted Robusta; the author prefers a medium-dark Arabica espresso blend. THE PAGE GIVES NO PEPPER-TO-COFFEE RATIO beyond this half teaspoon against 15 g.
ingredients: Water, enough to fill the AeroPress chamber at 200 °F, from at least 16 ounces boiled
equipment: AeroPress with fine metal or paper filter
steps: Toast the Selim pod and any optional spices in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until they release their aroma, avoiding burnt spots.
Grind the toasted spices in a spice grinder or mortar to about the size of the coffee grounds.
Bring at least 16 ounces of water to a boil. Put 15 g of medium-fine ground coffee and 1/2 teaspoon of the ground spice mix in the AeroPress.
Top it off with enough 200 °F water to fill the chamber and steep for 2 to 3 minutes. Press and drink.
chefTips: The one observable cue is the aroma of the toasting spices, not burnt.
The page prints no roasting temperature for the beans or the spices.
Traditional café Touba uses dark-roasted Robusta.
commonMistakes: Grinding the spices much coarser than the coffee.
Using the whole spice mix instead of the half teaspoon the brew step uses.
healthBenefits: Contains caffeine; the selim pod adds a peppery warmth.
culturalNote: A Western home-brew adaptation of a Mouride coffee. The pepper is the Selim pod (Xylopia aethiopica), djar in Wolof. The brotherhood tradition and the Grand Magal pilgrimage are documented in other sources, none of which is cited here.
sources: Byline as printed: Julia Bobak, Home Grounds. Published 16 August 2022, last updated 27 June 2025. Yield ‘One 8-ounce drink’. SINGLE-PASS.

Figures returned: 15 grams coffee, medium-fine; one Selim pod; optional 1 tsp grated nutmeg, 1 tsp coriander seeds, 1 cardamom pod; 1/2 tsp of the ground spice mix for the brew; 200 F water; ‘steep for 2 to 3 minutes’; cue ‘until they release their aroma, stirring occasionally to avoid developing burnt spots’. The article gives NO pepper-to-coffee ratio and no roast temperature for beans or spices.

UNRECONCILED, djar proportion, other printings (see SEN107): 2:1 coffee to ground pepper by weight (Dakaractu 2022); about 4:1 (Wikipedia); 10 g Selim to 40 g coffee (Barista Magazine, no date); 10 to 15 pods to 40 g coffee (ileauxepices.com); 3 pods to 50 g coffee (a spice retailer with no byline or date); 1 pod to 15 g coffee here. Pod counts cannot be converted to weight without a pod weight, which no source gives.
